claims.text: Under dynamic loading, HEAs derive superior strength and ductility from in situ grain refinement and local compositional homogenization.
Grain refinement and compositional homogenization enhance dislocation blocking while permitting dynamic recovery.
The initial HEA has a nanoscale grain structure.
The initial HEA has homogeneous grains and a homogeneous complex multi-element distribution.
Comparable lower-entropy alloys have coarser or less uniformly distributed grains.
Near but below the order-disorder transition temperature, diffusion remains active during dynamic deformation.
A moderate strain-rate regime permits dynamic grain refinement and dynamic recovery in HEAs.
Dynamic loading produces grain refinement in HEAs.
Dynamic loading causes transient elemental redistribution at grain boundaries.
Dynamic loading triggers local shear banding and cascading dislocation events.
Shear banding and cascading dislocation events subdivide grains and increase grain-boundary area.
The refined microstructure raises yield strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Continued dislocation motion and dynamic recovery preserve ductility despite grain refinement.
Dynamically loaded HEAs will have higher yield strength than lower-entropy baseline alloys.
Dynamically loaded HEAs will maintain or slightly improve ductility relative to lower-entropy baseline alloys.
In situ measurements during dynamic loading will show reduced grain size in the HEA.
In situ measurements during dynamic loading will show increased dislocation density in the HEA.
The proposed mechanism applies near but below the order-disorder transition temperature and at moderate strain rates where diffusion and dynamic recovery occur.
At temperatures or strain rates far outside the proposed window, alternative deformation mechanisms may dominate.
